reviews.scopeMarkdown: Bài gốc: **183 từ**, đếm bằng cách tách nguyên văn theo khoảng trắng; nằm trong yêu cầu 150–200 từ của lớp. Cô chỉ chấm Đề 1 đã gõ, chưa chấm Đề 2 hoặc bản scan.
reviews.overall: Em cần sửa và nộp lại. Bài vẫn còn lỗi dùng tên nước làm chủ thể biến động ở “Belgium also remained unchanged” và “Italy continued to rise”. Hai câu mở Detail cũng chưa nêu lại đầy đủ tỷ lệ phần trăm nữ nghị sĩ theo yêu cầu bài học. Em đã chọn được đỉnh của France, nhưng bỏ mốc cuối của nước này và lặp kết quả Italy ở hai đoạn. Em có dùng “before falling”, “reaching” và quy chiếu “the figure for France”; hãy vận dụng tiếp những cách đã học để sửa đúng chủ thể và tổ chức dữ liệu gọn hơn.
reviews.dataGrouping: Detail 1 nêu mức năm 2000 của cả năm nước, rồi theo dõi France đến 2008 và Italy, the UK đến 2012. Detail 2 bổ sung diễn biến Germany, Belgium và lặp lại kết quả cuối kỳ của Italy, nên cách mở bằng “the latter half” chưa thể hiện được hai nhóm thời gian rõ ràng. Cô giữ cách phân bố chính của em: Detail 1 vẫn có các mốc đầu cùng diễn biến France, Italy và the United Kingdom; Detail 2 hoàn tất diễn biến Germany và Belgium. Em chỉ cần bỏ ý Italy bị lặp và đổi lời chuyển đoạn cho khớp phần thông tin còn lại, theo C05.

reviews.originalEssay:
The line graph illustrates the percentages of female members of parliament in five European countries between 2000 and 2012.

Overall, there was a general increase in the percentages of female members of parliament in Germany, Italy, the UK and Belgium, while France experienced some fluctuations. Also, of note is that Italy had the highest figure in 2012, whereas the UK had the lowest figure in 2000.

To elaborate, in 2000, Germany had the highest percentage, at approximately 33%, followed by Italy and France, at around 26% and 25% respectively. Belgium and the UK had lower figures, at about 17% and 3%. The figure for France rose significantly to 37% in 2004, before falling to around 29% in 2008. Conversely, the percentages in Italy and the UK continued to increase, reaching approximately 39% and 28% respectively in 2012.

Regarding the latter half of the provided timeline, the figure for Germany remained relatively stable, increasing slightly to around 36% in 2012. Belgium also remained unchanged at approximately 28% from 2004 onwards. Finally, Italy continued to rise, reaching the highest figure of about 39% in 2012.

reviews.originalEssay:
The pie charts illustrate the main reasons why students chose a particular university in the UK in 1997 and 2007.

Overall, suitable degree courses were the most important reason in both years. Also, of note is that the percentage of students choosing a university because of its proximity to their parental home increased significantly, while good sports and social activities became much less important.

To elaborate, in 1997, suitable degree courses accounted for the highest figure, at 35%, followed by the quality of resources, at 21%. Good sports and social activities and quality of teaching made up 19% and 15% respectively, while proximity to parental home had the lowest figure, at only 10%. In 2007, suitable degree courses still ranked first, rising slightly to 37%. The figure for proximity to parental home, conversely, increased significantly to 22%.

Regarding the other reasons, the percentage of students choosing a university because of the quality of resources decreased from 21% in 1997 to 17% in 2007. Meanwhile, quality of teaching rose slightly from 15% to 18%. Finally, good sports and social activities experienced a considerable decline, falling from 19% to just 6% in 2007.

The table shows the number of universities ranked in the world’s top 200 in three subjects in five countries in 2011.

Overall, the USA had the highest numbers in all three subjects, while New Zealand had the lowest figures. Biology was the most popular subject in the USA and the UK, whereas psychology had the highest numbers in Australia and Canada.

Finally, New Zealand had the lowest numbers overall. There were only 6 universities in biology, 2 in medicine and 4 in psychology. These figures were much lower than those of the other four countries.
